subject.title: [Bug]: Browser interactions can exhaust model context by injecting too much page content

question: Should OpenClaw make compact, goal-shaped browser reads the default for interactive browser tasks, and which explicit raw/full escape hatch should remain?
rationale: Current main already has caps, efficient mode, compact role snapshots, compact action results, and generic tool-result truncation, but changing the default browser read contract affects ref completeness and existing automation behavior.

options.title: Compact default with raw escape hatch
options.body: Make the default browser read compact and actionable while preserving explicit full AI/ARIA reads for complete page-state workflows.

options.title: Keep efficient mode opt-in
options.body: Leave defaults unchanged and rely on mode=efficient, maxChars, selectors, and generic truncation for context-heavy workflows.

options.title: Fold into browser field report
options.body: Track this under the broader browser automation field-report umbrella if maintainers want one coordinated design for action diffs, stale refs, viewport reads, and context shaping.

recommendation.title: Compact default with raw escape hatch
recommendation.body: Make the default browser read compact and actionable while preserving explicit full AI/ARIA reads for complete page-state workflows.

likelyOwner.reason: The remaining choice is a browser plugin product/API contract decision, and the history sample points to steipete as the strongest browser-boundary owner.
